controls.label: Color
controls.qualification: Colour from Gaia's spectrum of the star. The disc itself is unresolved.
controls.notes: The colour of Gaia DR3's measured spectrum of the star: a slightly blue-white F-type dwarf. No image of the photosphere exists, and its spin axis is not measured; the display axis is celestial north.

controls.label: Debris ring · JWST 1.8 µm
controls.notes: The star in its Gaia colour, with the ring of debris around it as JWST/NIRCam imaged it at 1.8 micrometres (F182M) behind a coronagraph on 11 October 2023 (programme 2780). It is drawn in the colours and on the logarithmic scale Gáspár et al. (2026) print it in, their Figure 26, and seen from Earth it matches their panel: the ring's long axis within about a degree of theirs, the same axis ratio, and the same fall of brightness from the ring into its halo. The ring is starlight scattered by dust, about 81 au in radius and tilted 29° from face-on. The image has no third axis, so the depth is inferred: a tilted ring of the measured geometry projects to it better than a spherical shell or the constant depth an extrusion assumes, and each line of sight is placed on it. Which side is nearer to us and how thick the ring is are stated conventions. The colours are a legend for brightness, not the colour of the dust, and the ring is drawn darker than the printed figure so that it stays see-through. Nothing is drawn within 1″ of the star, where the starlight left after subtraction outweighs the dust.
